title: ClaimAccount
description: device -> server, sent on an established (challenge-verified) connection to claim this device for a signed-in account (design doc D-33). The connection itself proves possession of the device's Keystore key, the same pattern regenerate_secret uses, so the message carries no device identifier of its own. account_token is a short-lived, single-use token the app's own backend-facing session mints right after Google sign-in completes (POST /accounts/claim-token) — not the OAuth access token itself, so a leaked claim token can't be replayed for anything beyond the one claim it was minted for. install_hint is Android's per-app device ID (ANDROID_ID); the server keeps only a keyed hash of it and uses it to recognise the same phone after a reinstall. replace_device_id, when present, claims this phone in place of the account's device with that id: that device is retired and, if it is connected, its connection is closed with WS close code 4004 ("replaced" — CLOSE_REPLACED, exported from this package).

install_hint.description: Android's per-app device ID (ANDROID_ID); the server keeps only a keyed hash of it and uses it to recognise the same phone after a reinstall.

replace_device_id.description: Claim this phone in place of the account's device with this id. That device is retired and, if connected, its connection is closed with WS close code 4004 ("replaced"). A device_id that isn't one of the account's phones is rejected with claim_rejected reason "unknown_device".
